# Head of Security
The Head of Security is the commander of the station's Security forces.
1. Standard [color=#00a933]Code Green[/color] equipment is:
or
2. The standard Command SOP applies with the exception of section 6, which is overridden by the listed equipment above.
3. When patrolling, you must follow all Security Officer protocols and comply with permitted equipment levels. You may not carry more than one sidearm. The WT550 and Proto-5x are considered sidearms for this purpose.
4. You are responsible for your staff and are expected to coordinate and delegate roles to your personnel as necessary. Remember, if you are not the sole officer in the Security Department, then you are [color=#ff0000]not[/color] to do everything yourself.
5. You may [color=#ff0000]not[/color] utilise the Armory for your own benefit, and any equipment you use must be for the appropriate alert level. If your equipment requires a permit for use, then you [color=#ff0000]must[/color] fill a permit and have it on person.
6. Issued permits may [color=#ff0000]not[/color] be for your own benefit, and must have justifiable reason behind them. You may [color=#ff0000]not[/color] issue permits for [color=#8d281e]highly illegal contraband[/color] [color=#ff0000]whatsoever[/color].
6. You may authorise the Warden with [color=#ffe100]Command comms[/color] (using the spare headset in your locker) if you believe it to be beneficial for them to have. You may [color=#ff0000]not[/color] authorise any interim Warden in this manner, nor any other member of the department.
## Additional Duties
NanoTrasen Research Stations in your sector are often short-staffed, and as such your skills and qualifications may necessitate you take on extra responsibilities. This section of the SOP will cover what duties fall to you in lieu of dedicated personnel.
1. You are expected to fulfill the duties of the Warden, Detective, and Brigmedic in that order of priority if you do not have personnel available. You are also expected to follow [color=#ffe100]all relevant SOP[/color] for these roles when acting in their capacity.
2. If you have rank-and-file Officers that express interests in taking on responsibilities associated with these roles, you should [color=#00a933]delegate[/color] the work to them. A full field promotion is [color=#ffe100]highly recommended[/color] if time is not of the essence.
3. Warden duties should be your [color=#ffe100]priority[/color] secondary only to your own, and in the absence of a Warden you should prioritise the integrity of the department. It may be necessary to adjust or limit your patrol schedule to accomodate for this.
4. Detective duties permit use of all Detective equipment for forensics and interrogation purposes. You may [color=#ff0000]not[/color] go undercover when acting as a Detective.
5. Brigmedic duties should only involve preparing basic chemical treatment. You should not be aiming to stock the entire bay as the Head of Security. You may [color=#00a933]forego Brigmedic duties[/color] entirely if you are unfamiliar with chemical synthesis, or there are more pressing matters to attend to.
## Sentencing and Prisoner Oversight
The Head of Security is responsible for overseeing sentencing in the absence of a Warden, and is expected to provide oversight of the process even with one. This section of the SOP will detail your powers and responsibilities in this regard.
1. You [color=#ff0000]must[/color] ensure that you and the Warden are aware of every sentencing, and that every arrest comes with a report unless there is threat of imminent station destruction.
2. You may [color=#00a933]parole cooperative prisoners[/color] sentenced for non-violent crimes at your discretion, provided the department is made aware and the SOP for such a procedure is followed.
3. You may [color=#ffe100]overrule any sentence[/color] that is not assigned by an official NT Magistrate, but [color=#ff0000]not[/color] for prisoners who have already had their sentences read to them.
